abstracts.abstract: Requires the board of elections to publish notice of a polling place location change thirty days before the change or on the earliest known date of such change in the event of an emergency; provides for the use of electronic mail to notify voters of polling place location changes.

bill.title: Relates to providing notice of polling place location changes

posted_text:
🗳️ NY A11708 — You'll Get a Mailer About Your Polling Place Changes

New York will require boards of elections to send voters a written notice by mail at least 60 days before an election or registration day if they change a polling place.

The board must also post the change on its website within 30 days.

If the board has a voter’s email address, it can send a separate electronic notice, but this won’t replace the required mailer.

The law also says the board must use an alternative form of notice if mailing isn’t possible, and provides a way for the board to quickly post changes if a polling place becomes unusable unexpectedly.

Sept. 2, 2026: Referred to Election Law.

🔗 Read the full bill: https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/bills/2025/A11708
